The Government Pension Fund Global, known as the oil fund, is the fund where Norway saves its oil income. Set up by law in 1990, it is the largest sovereign wealth fund in the world.

After Ekofisk, Norway feared the fate of other oil states: inflation, ruined industry and waste. Instead the state puts its oil revenue into the fund and invests it abroad, owning a small share of almost every listed company in the world. The government may spend only about the expected return each year.

The fund is worth more than a quarter of a million dollars for every Norwegian. Ethics rules bar investment in makers of some weapons and in tobacco. It has become a model for other countries with natural wealth, unlike the resource curse seen elsewhere. See Norway.
